items.label: Largest hemorrhage diameter (A)
items.subtitle: Greatest diameter on the axial CT slice with the largest hemorrhage area.

items.label: Perpendicular diameter (B)
items.subtitle: Largest diameter perpendicular (90°) to A on the same axial slice.

items.label: Weighted slice count
items.subtitle: Sum of CT slices showing hemorrhage (1 = >75% area, 0.5 = 25–75% area, 0 = <25% area).

items.label: CT slice thickness
items.subtitle: Thickness of each axial CT slice (commonly 0.5 cm / 5 mm).

metadata.name: ABC/2 for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) volume
metadata.summary: Ellipsoid approximation formula for estimating parenchymal hematoma volume on non-contrast head CT.
clinical_pearls: Excludes intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and subarachnoid extension.
Always measure length (A) and perpendicular width (B) accurately on the axial CT slice with the largest hemorrhage area.

Pitfall — Irregular or warfarin-related ICH: For lobar, irregular, or multilobed hemorrhages (including warfarin-related ICH), ABC/2 may overestimate volume compared with computer-assisted planimetry (Huttner et al., 2006).

references.citation: Kothari RU, Brott T, Broderick JP, et al. The ABCs of measuring intracerebral hemorrhage volumes. Stroke. 1996;27(8):1304-1305.

Huttner HB, Steiner T, Hartmann M, et al. Comparison of ABC/2 estimation technique to computer-assisted planimetric analysis in warfarin-related intracerebral parenchymal hemorrhage. Stroke. 2006;37(2):404-408.

interpretation.label: Small-to-Moderate Volume (< 30 mL)
interpretation.summary: Hematoma volume < 30 mL (0 points on the ICH Score volume component).

interpretation.label: Large Volume (30 – 59.9 mL)
interpretation.summary: Hematoma volume >= 30 mL (adds 1 point on the ICH Score; monitor closely for herniation).

interpretation.label: Massive Volume (>= 60 mL)
interpretation.summary: Hematoma volume >= 60 mL; high risk of mass effect and early neurological deterioration.

assessment_guides.title: Kothari Slice-Weighting Rule (C)
bedside_steps: Compare each axial slice containing blood to the reference slice with the largest hemorrhage area.
Assign 1.0 if area is > 75% of the largest slice, 0.5 if 25–75%, and 0 if < 25%.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Counting small cap slices as 1.0 instead of 0.5 or 0 systematically overestimates ICH volume.
Do not include isolated intraventricular blood when measuring A, B, or C.
